title: He had everything… and still lost it.
paragraphs: He had everything… and still lost it.
A throne. Authority. Anointing.
But Saul chose disobedience over surrender—and everything changed.
Let’s confront the moment that unsettles many readers:
“An evil spirit from the Lord tormented him.” (1 Samuel 16:14)
Why would God allow that?
The Real Story Behind the Torment
This wasn’t random cruelty.
This was consequence.
Saul had already rejected God—repeatedly.

• He disobeyed direct commands (1 Samuel 13, 15)
• He feared people more than God
• He refused true repentance
So God did something terrifying:
He lifted His Spirit from Saul.
And when the Spirit of the Lord departed… something else filled the vacuum.

Not because God became evil—
But because Saul chose distance from the only source of peace.
Judgment Isn’t Always Fire—Sometimes It’s Withdrawal
We expect judgment to look like lightning.
But sometimes?

It looks like silence.
Confusion.
Inner torment.
God gave Saul what he insisted on:
Life without Him.
And that’s where the torment lived.
The Spiritual Principle Most People Miss
God didn’t create evil in Saul.
He removed protection.
And when divine covering lifts, the human heart—already bent by sin—becomes vulnerable.
This is echoed later in Scripture:

• God “gave them over” (Romans 1:24)
• Not forced… but permitted
Saul’s torment was not just spiritual—it was the exposure of a heart that refused God.
And Then… David Enters the Story
While Saul is unraveling…
God raises David.
A shepherd. A worshiper.
When David played music, the torment lifted.
Why?
Because the presence of God still drives out darkness.
Even in a king who rejected Him.
This Isn’t Just Saul’s Story
This is a warning.

You can be anointed… and still fall.
You can be chosen… and still drift.
You can know truth… and still resist it.
Sin doesn’t always destroy instantly.
Sometimes it erodes—quietly, internally—until peace is gone.
But Here’s the Gospel Saul Missed
Where Saul hardened his heart…
Jesus Christ came to restore broken ones.
Saul ran from God.
Jesus runs toward sinners.
Saul refused repentance.
Jesus calls you into it.
Because torment is not your destiny.
Redemption is.
The Turning Point You Still Have
You are not too far gone.
But you are not safe in disobedience either.

Sin leads to separation.
Separation invites darkness.
But repentance?
It brings you back into the presence of God.
And in His presence…
There is peace again.
Reflection
Where in your life have you been resisting God’s voice?
“Lord, I choose obedience over pride.”
Send this to someone who needs to understand what distance from God really costs.
You’ll need this reminder when conviction comes again.
Shame doesn’t get the final word.
We Write Stories that Shame Tried to Erase.
